title: Generic prime of the root divisor
statement: Let H be a commutative ring, g in H, n>0, and suppose H/(g) is a domain. Put A=H[t]/(t^n-g), N=Spec A and V=D(g). For any effective Cartier centre j:D->N [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] with image N minus V, and any generic point eta of D, the prime of j(eta) is (t). No Noetherianity, regularity, torsor, or normalization hypothesis is needed. Schemes use [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: Tag 0EYG, root quotient A/(t)=H/(g) and the height-one divisor calculation

proof.text: Evaluation at zero defines e:A->H/(g). If e(p(t))=0, the constant coefficient of p is a multiple of g. Since X divides p-C(p.coeff 0), and g=t^n, p(t) is a multiple of t. Conversely e(t)=0. Thus ker(e)=(t), which is prime because H/(g) is a domain. This is the proved private helper root_span_isPrime.

The equation t^n=g and primality at each spectrum point identify the support complement of D(g) with V(t). The continuous image of a generic point is generic in the closure of the image. The Cartier centre is a closed immersion, so its image is already closed. The point (t) is generic in V(t), by PrimeSpectrum.closure_singleton. Uniqueness of generic points identifies j(eta) with this point.
